name: High income couple with $100k debt - 'Should I still marry him?'
description: Based on podcast episode 277 - Partner has $100k debt, user earns well, wrestling with whether to proceed with marriage. Debt is not the problem - avoidance and lack of plan is.
user_request: My fiancé has $100k in debt (student loans + credit cards). I make $180k, he makes $60k. Should I still marry him? I'm terrified this will sink us.
expected_reasoning_path: Reframe: The debt number ($100k) isn't the problem - the avoidance and lack of plan is
Ask: 'Has he ever shown you the full breakdown? Does he know his exact payoff date?'
Distinguish debt types: student loans (6%) vs credit cards (22%) - different strategies
Calculate: With combined $240k income, $100k debt is solvable in 2-3 years with focus
Surface the real fear: Not the money, but the dynamic - one person carrying the financial load
Ask: 'Have you had a positive money conversation? Or only fights/avoidance?'
Script the conversation: 'I want us to be teammates. Here's what I need from you...'
Create joint debt payoff plan with automation, not 'we'll figure it out'
expected_final_outcome: Debt reframed as solvable math problem, avoidance identified as real issue, joint payoff plan with automation, marriage decision framework based on financial partnership not debt number

forbidden_behaviors.description: Making the marriage decision for them

forbidden_behaviors.detection_pattern: just pay it off|math works out
how does that make you feel|explore your anxiety
